judgment.rationale: The report says Thunderbird 115.14.0 is identified as Explorer in Workspaces 0.84.1, so launch opens the wrong window. A closed sibling #34599 was cross-referenced to broader app-detection issue #34558, which received Workspaces 0.85 work for Discord/Steam and other applications, but there is no evidence that Thunderbird was fixed. Request a current-build confirmation rather than design a competing detection change.
evidence: The report lists Workspaces 0.84.1, Thunderbird 115.14.0, and says creating a workspace detects it as Explorer.
Issue #34599 is closed and its commenter links it to #34558, but it contains no Thunderbird-specific fix confirmation.
The broader #34558 issue was worked on during the 0.85 development cycle; merged PRs #34602, #34627, and #34640 address Discord/Steam detection, not explicitly Thunderbird.
The selected issue has one automated similarity comment for #34599 and no maintainer response.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether Thunderbird is still misidentified on a current supported build; if so, request the exact Thunderbird window type and a short capture/launch sequence before deciding on code changes.

fix_assessment.rationale: Related Workspaces app-detection changes exist, but none establishes that Thunderbird's Explorer misidentification is fixed. Do not propose a competing implementation until current behavior is known.

issue_context.summary: Workspaces reportedly classifies Thunderbird as Explorer, so launching a captured workspace opens File Explorer in its place.
known_information: The report used PowerToys 0.84.1 and Thunderbird 115.14.0 64-bit, with Workspaces running as administrator.
The author provides only 'Create workspace' as reproduction steps and says Thunderbird was not detected correctly.
The related #34599 was closed as part of broader app-detection discussion #34558.
Merged PRs #34602, #34627, and #34640 address Discord and Steam detection, but do not document a Thunderbird-specific correction.
inferences: The incorrect Explorer classification could be related to process/window matching, but the issue does not show the detected executable or window identity.
The 0.85 work may have changed the broader detection path, so a current-version check must precede any new design.
issue_context.analysis: First establish whether the current release still misidentifies Thunderbird. If so, capture the actual window and process identity to distinguish a stale issue from a new Thunderbird-specific matching defect.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live body and the automated similarity comment.
Checked #34599 and #34558 plus merged detection PR titles; related work covers other applications and is not proof of a Thunderbird fix.

information_gaps.information: Whether Thunderbird is still shown as Explorer and launches incorrectly on the current supported PowerToys build.
information_gaps.why_needed: The report is from PowerToys 0.84.1 and Workspaces app-detection changes shipped in the 0.85 cycle.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please update to the current supported version, create a workspace containing Thunderbird, and confirm what application name appears in the captured list and what opens on launch.

information_gaps.information: If still failing, whether the misidentified window is Thunderbird's main window or a child/dialog window, and whether it runs elevated.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes process matching from a transient or elevated window mismatch.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please state whether the main Thunderbird window was open during capture and whether Thunderbird was launched with administrator privileges.

actions.label: Confirm Thunderbird detection on current build

comment.body:
The issue says Thunderbird 115.14.0 was identified as Explorer in Workspaces 0.84.1, but Workspaces app-detection changes shipped afterward. Could you confirm:
- Whether a current supported PowerToys build still lists Thunderbird as Explorer and opens File Explorer when launching the workspace.
- If it still fails, whether the Thunderbird main window was open at capture time and whether Thunderbird was elevated.
This will distinguish an unresolved Thunderbird case from the earlier broader detection work without proposing a duplicate fix.
